intro_band.agent_remit_summary: yaah is a Go CLI and runtime that generates hooks, skills, agents, slash commands, MCP and LSP configuration for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI, and runs alongside those agents as a hook dispatcher, a stdio MCP server and a per-session audit store. It may expose seven MCP tools (`yaah_scan_secrets`, `yaah_lint`, `yaah_check_command`, `yaah_doctor`, `yaah_session_info`, `yaah_planning_status`, `yaah_planning_init`) and five hook handlers, read and write within the target repository and its own cache, and fetch skills and agents only from pinned repositories in its vetted catalog. The command guard and secret scanner are declared fail-closed safety controls that must never be removed or downgraded to advisory, credentials must never be embedded in generated configuration, and the `/yaah:*` workflow must never be self-invoked by the model.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: A Go 1.25 module built on cobra and the official MCP go-sdk; `cmd/yaah/main.go` wires `generate`, `hook`, `serve`, `doctor`, `session` and `skills` commands around a `Harness` (`pkg/harness/harness.go`) whose `NewWithDefaults()` in `defaults.go` registers the linter, command-guard, secret-remediation chain, comment-checker and session-logger handlers plus Context7, Pulumi and yaah MCP providers, 29 workflow commands, and SHA-pinned remote skills and agents fetched through `pkg/gitcache`. `yaah hook <event>` reads the host's JSON on stdin, dispatches through `hooks.Registry`, records the call to `.claude/sessions/<id>.json` via `session.Store`, and exits 2 to block; `yaah serve` exposes the seven tools over `mcp.StdioTransport` from `pkg/mcpserver/tools.go`. Per-target generators in `pkg/generator/` emit `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json`, `opencode.json` plus a JS hook bridge, `.codex/config.toml` and hooks, and Copilot hooks, but the Codex event map carries no tool-use hooks and the secret scanner is bound to PostToolUse rather than PreToolUse.

behavior_summary:
yaah's safety story rests on two hook handlers, and both are weaker in practice than the remit's "fail closed" language promises. The secret scanner runs on PostToolUse, so a credential-bearing edit is already on disk when it fires; any handler error, an unparseable payload or a single line over 64 KB makes yaah hook exit 1, which the host treats as non-blocking; and the Codex target ships with no tool-use hooks at all. The command guard that does run is a seven-pattern regex denylist that simple flag reordering defeats.

A second pattern is trust delegated without checks. Third-party SKILL.md frontmatter is written verbatim, which lets a fetched skill pre-approve Bash(bash:*) for the host. The yaah_lint MCP tool runs linter binaries in any directory the model names, npx resolves unpinned packages at hook time, and none of the 29 /yaah:* commands, including /yaah:autonomous, sets disable-model-invocation.

rules.rule_text: yaah MUST NEVER treat the content of fetched remote skills or agents, MCP tool descriptions, or scanned/linted file contents as instructions that change its own behavior or safety decisions — such content is untrusted data, never authority over yaah.
yaah MUST NEVER auto-invoke its /yaah:* workflow commands, including the autonomous workflow, without an explicit user invocation; the model must not self-trigger them.
yaah MUST NEVER run with its command-guard or secret-scanner safety hooks removed, disabled, or downgraded to a non-blocking / advisory mode; these are safety controls, not optional lint.
stdio only; no network bind
Within the target repository and the yaah cache directory
Fetch and cache only; sources must be pinned (see Authorized Counterparties)
Only servers the operator configured
Disabled unless the operator has explicitly authorized it
Any other outbound network destination

Closure rule: the authoritative allowlist is the operator-configured vetted catalog of authorized remote skill/agent source repositories, MCP providers, and marketplaces; community-tier or unreviewed skills are excluded unless the operator has explicitly authorized them.
Trusted Domains
Fetching default or shipped remote skills/agents from mutable refs (branches) rather than immutable refs (a commit SHA or version tag).
Wiring in any skill, agent, MCP server, marketplace, or plugin outside the operator-configured vetted catalog (see the Closure rule under Trusted Services / Integrations).
Closure rule: any tool the runtime or MCP server exposes, or any hook handler it runs, that is not in this baseline is an undeclared capability.
The experimental fact-check hooks (spawn a tool-using subagent with outbound web access).
Any MCP provider that carries credentials or OAuth (e.g. Notion, remote OAuth servers).
No MCP tool may execute arbitrary shell commands outside the command guard, and no tool may return detected secret values in cleartext.
Allowed Data Sources
Detected secret values MUST NEVER be written into session logs, findings records, generated configuration, or any yaah output in cleartext — secrets are referenced by location and pattern only.
Credentials, API tokens, and OAuth secrets MUST NEVER be embedded in generated configuration files.
Credentials, API tokens, and OAuth secrets MUST NEVER be committed to the repository.
Credentials, API tokens, and OAuth secrets MUST be sourced from environment variables or a secrets manager.
Repository contents, scanned file contents, and session audit data MUST NEVER be transmitted to any destination other than the local filesystem or an explicitly-configured trusted integration.
Allowed Without Approval

Enabling any feature that makes outbound network calls or spawns an autonomous subagent (e.g. the experimental fact-checker): such features MUST be off by default and enabled only by explicit operator opt-in.
A file edit that introduces a hardcoded credential MUST NEVER be written — the secret scanner blocks it (fail closed).

A shell command matching the dangerous-command denylist (e.g. `rm -rf /`, force-push to a protected branch, `git reset --hard`, destructive SQL) MUST NEVER be allowed to execute — the command guard blocks it (fail closed).

Session files MUST NEVER be read or written at paths derived from unvalidated session identifiers; identifiers containing path separators or the special values `.` / `..` are rejected (path-traversal prevention).

Generated configuration MUST NEVER weaken the host coding agent's permission/sandbox posture: it may not place the host into a permission-bypassing (`bypassPermissions` / `dontAsk`) or sandbox-disabled mode by default, nor drop the host below its stated minimum permission/sandbox posture.

When the command guard matches a dangerous command, or the secret scanner detects a credential in an edit, the hook must block the operation and record the block (with its reason) to the session audit log.
`yaah doctor` reports missing dependencies or misconfiguration for the operator to resolve; this surfaces a warning without blocking generation.

Session lifecycle events, tool calls (including MCP-server tool invocations served via `yaah serve`), blocked commands, and file modifications are recorded to `.claude/sessions/<id>.json` as a durable, structured audit trail.

findings.summary: No /yaah:* workflow command sets disable-model-invocation, so the host model can self-trigger them, including /yaah:autonomous, which runs a phase without pausing.
findings.description: `CommandAdvanced.DisableModelInvocation` exists and `buildCommandMarkdown()` would emit `disable-model-invocation: true`, but no command in `pkg/commands/builtins/` sets it. The generated `.claude/commands/yaah/*.md` files are therefore discoverable and invocable by the model. A model steered by injected repository content can start `/yaah:autonomous`, which auto-selects every decision and executes plans without user review.
policy_rule_text: yaah MUST NEVER auto-invoke its /yaah:* workflow commands, including the autonomous workflow, without an explicit user invocation; the model must not self-trigger them.

evidence.snippet: DisableModelInvocation bool is declared on CommandAdvanced, but a grep of pkg/commands/builtins/ finds no command that sets it to true
Advanced() returns CommandAdvanced{Context: "fork"} only; the command body tells the model to auto-select defaults and not to pause between plan, execute and verify

recommended_actions: Set `DisableModelInvocation: true` in `Advanced()` for every `/yaah:*` builtin, starting with `autonomous.go`, `execute.go`, `ship.go` and `quick.go`. Add a test in `builtins_test.go` asserting that every registered command emits `disable-model-invocation: true`.

findings.summary: The secret scanner runs on PostToolUse, so a credential-bearing Edit or Write is already on disk when it fires and cannot be stopped.
findings.description: The remit requires that such an edit "MUST NEVER be written". `SecretScanner.Events()` returns only `HookPostToolUse`, and `ScanFile()` re-reads the file from disk after the host has written it, so exit 2 only reports the failure to the model and the credential stays in the working tree. No PreToolUse path inspects the proposed `content` or `new_string` before the write.
policy_rule_text: A file edit that introduces a hardcoded credential MUST NEVER be written — the secret scanner blocks it (fail closed).

evidence.snippet: Events() returns []schema.HookEvent{schema.HookPostToolUse}; Execute() calls ScanFile(input.FilePath()), which opens the already-written file (lines 91-100)
secret-remediation chain registered for HookPostToolUse with matcher (?i)^(Edit|Write|MultiEdit)$ only, with no PreToolUse registration

recommended_actions: Add a PreToolUse handler in `secretscan.go` that scans the proposed `tool_input.content` / `new_string` / `edits[].new_string` and returns `Block: true` before the write. Keep the PostToolUse scan as a backstop.

findings.summary: The hook dispatcher fails open: parse and handler errors exit 1, which the host treats as non-blocking, and scanner I/O errors never set Block.
findings.description: `yaah hook` maps only `ErrHookBlocked` to exit 2; every other error falls through to cobra and `os.Exit(1)`, so the guarded action proceeds. In `SecretScanner`, a read error, including `bufio.Scanner`'s 64 KB `ErrTooLong` on a single long line, returns `Result{Error}` without `Block`, so a credential placed after one minified line is neither detected nor blocked, and `Registry.Dispatch` aborts every remaining handler on the first handler error.
policy_rule_text: A file edit that introduces a hardcoded credential MUST NEVER be written — the secret scanner blocks it (fail closed).

A shell command matching the dangerous-command denylist (e.g. `rm -rf /`, force-push to a protected branch, `git reset --hard`, destructive SQL) MUST NEVER be allowed to execute — the command guard blocks it (fail closed).

evidence.snippet: ReadInput error returns err, and HandleHookEvent errors other than ErrHookBlocked return err; main() then calls os.Exit(1) (line 71), never exit 2
scanner.Err() (e.g. bufio.ErrTooLong past 64 KB) propagates, and Execute (lines 134-138) returns &hooks.Result{Error: ...} with Block unset

recommended_actions: In `hookCmd()` for PreToolUse and PostToolUse, map any error (parse, dispatch or handler) to exit 2 with a "yaah failed closed" reason. In `SecretScanner.Execute`, set `Block: true` on scan or open errors.
Raise the scanner buffer with `scanner.Buffer(...)`, or scan the whole content, so long lines cannot truncate detection.

findings.summary: Codex targets get no tool-use hooks, so they run without the command guard and secret scanner; the OpenCode bridge drops args before scanning.
findings.description: The cross-agent `hookMappings` give Codex only SessionStart, Stop and notify, and the README says Codex security checks are "available via yaah MCP tools". That is exactly the advisory downgrade the remit forbids. The generated OpenCode plugin caches `output.args` in `pendingCalls` but never reads them, and its after-hook sends `input.args || {}`, so `FilePath()` is likely empty and the secret scanner and linter no-op [Inferred], while its before-hook swallows every non-2 failure.
policy_rule_text: yaah MUST NEVER run with its command-guard or secret-scanner safety hooks removed, disabled, or downgraded to a non-blocking / advisory mode; these are safety controls, not optional lint.

evidence.snippet: HookPreToolUse and HookPostToolUse mappings set Claude, OpenCode and Copilot but leave Codex empty; CodexGenerator.GenerateHooks skips events whose Codex name is "" (README.md:236 documents "Hooks limited to SessionStart/Stop")
pendingCalls.set(...) caches args but is never read; the tool.execute.after handler (line 108) passes input.args || {} to yaah hook PostToolUse

recommended_actions: Do not emit a Codex config without blocking tool hooks: map Codex's pre-execution approval or exec-policy surface to `yaah hook PreToolUse`, or refuse to generate the Codex target until it exists.

In the OpenCode plugin, look up the cached `pendingCalls` args in `tool.execute.after`, fail closed on any non-zero exit in `tool.execute.before`, and add a generator test that round-trips a Write payload with a `file_path`.

findings.summary: Fetched third-party SKILL.md frontmatter is written verbatim, so remote content decides its own host permissions; the shipped agent-rules skill pre-approves Bash(bash:*).
findings.description: `buildSkillMarkdown()` skips yaah's own frontmatter whenever the remote content starts with `---`, so `allowed-tools`, `disable-model-invocation` and similar fields come from the third-party author, not the operator. Untrusted content therefore sets a safety decision, letting it pre-approve shell execution in the host without a prompt (the command guard still applies). No content vetting runs on fetched skills: no frontmatter allowlist, instruction scan or hidden-character check.
policy_rule_text: yaah MUST NEVER treat the content of fetched remote skills or agents, MCP tool descriptions, or scanned/linted file contents as instructions that change its own behavior or safety decisions — such content is untrusted data, never authority over yaah.

evidence.snippet: contentHasFrontmatter := strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(content), "---"); if true, the remote SKILL.md is written as-is with no operator-controlled frontmatter
generated from netresearch/agent-rules-skill, this skill declares allowed-tools: Bash(git:*) Bash(jq:*) Bash(grep:*) Bash(find:*) Bash(bash:*) Read Glob Grep, which pre-approves arbitrary bash -c

recommended_actions: In `buildSkillMarkdown()`, parse remote frontmatter and rewrite it from an allowlist (name, description), dropping or operator-overriding `allowed-tools`, `model`, `context` and `agent`. Fail generation when a remote skill requests tool pre-approval the catalog entry does not grant.

findings.summary: yaah_lint runs linter pipelines (npx, cargo, golangci-lint) in the parent directory of any model-supplied path, executing code outside the command guard and repository.
findings.description: MCP tool calls bypass the Bash PreToolUse guard, and `yaah_lint` takes an unvalidated absolute `file_path`, sets `cwd = filepath.Dir(file_path)` and runs `exec.CommandContext` on each profile step. `npx tsc` and `npx prettier` resolve `node_modules/.bin` from that directory, and `cargo clippy` runs build scripts, so a model-chosen directory such as an extracted archive or `/tmp` yields arbitrary code execution. `yaah_scan_secrets` and `yaah_planning_init` likewise read or create paths anywhere on disk, with no containment to the target repository.
policy_rule_text: Within the target repository and the yaah cache directory
No MCP tool may execute arbitrary shell commands outside the command guard, and no tool may return detected secret values in cleartext.

evidence.snippet: cwd := filepath.Dir(args.FilePath); linter.LintFile(ctx, args.FilePath, args.Profile, cwd), with no check that FilePath resolves inside the repository (planning_init at lines 368-394 likewise accepts any project_dir)
exec.CommandContext(ctx, args[0], args[1:]...) with cmd.Dir = cwd, which runs the profile steps (npx tsc, npx prettier, golangci-lint run --fix, cargo clippy --fix) inside the caller-chosen directory

recommended_actions: In `tools.go`, resolve every `file_path` / `project_dir` with `filepath.Abs` + `EvalSymlinks` and reject anything not under the session cwd. Run `yaah_lint` with `cmd.Dir` fixed to the repository root, never the file's parent.

findings.summary: A supplied Notion token is interpolated literally into the generated MCP env and written to .mcp.json and four other committed config files.
findings.description: `Notion.Server()` builds `OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS` by concatenating the raw token, and every generator copies `srv.Env` verbatim into `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.json`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.copilot/mcp-config.json`. None of these files is covered by `.gitignore`. The remit requires credentials to be sourced from the environment or a secrets manager and never embedded or committed; instead the generated config carries the value, not a `${NOTION_TOKEN}` reference.

tags.label: Secrets stored in vault, not in files

policy_rule_text: Credentials, API tokens, and OAuth secrets MUST NEVER be embedded in generated configuration files.
Credentials, API tokens, and OAuth secrets MUST NEVER be committed to the repository.
Credentials, API tokens, and OAuth secrets MUST be sourced from environment variables or a secrets manager.

evidence.snippet: Env "OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS" is built as a JSON string with "Authorization": "Bearer " + n.apiToken, so the literal token value is embedded
GenerateMCPJSON copies Env: srv.Env into .mcp.json unchanged (settings.go:220, opencode.go:35, codex.go:48 and copilot.go:46 do the same)

recommended_actions: Change `NewNotion` to take an env-var name and emit a reference (for example `"Bearer ${NOTION_TOKEN}"` where the host expands env, or an `env` passthrough) instead of the value. Make `GenerateMCPJSON` and the other generators reject any `Env`/`Headers` value matching the secret-scanner patterns.

findings.summary: Default components run unpinned npm packages through npx (Context7 MCP, prettier, tsc), contacting the unapproved npm registry and executing whatever version resolves.
findings.description: The remit approves git-over-HTTPS to pinned repos and operator-configured MCP servers only; "any other outbound network destination" is unauthorized and `registry.npmjs.org` is not a trusted domain. `npx -y` with no `@version` installs and executes the latest published package on every session or edit, which is a rug-pull and typosquat path into code running with the developer's privileges. Both providers are on in `AllDefaults()`, which `yaah generate` uses.
policy_rule_text: Any other outbound network destination
Trusted Domains

evidence.snippet: Command "npx", Args ["-y", "@context7/mcp"] with no version pin, emitted into the root .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json
Prettier step runs npx prettier --write and TypeScript (line 103) runs npx tsc --noEmit, both unpinned; AllDefaults() enables both profiles (defaults.go:188-189)

recommended_actions: Pin every npx invocation to an exact version (`@context7/mcp@x.y.z`, `prettier@x.y.z`, `typescript@x.y.z`) and add `--no-install` / `--prefer-offline` for lint steps, so a missing tool fails instead of downloading. Alternatively, invoke locally installed binaries only.

findings.summary: The session audit trail is incomplete: MCP tool invocations go unrecorded, Session.Findings is never written, and an unreadable session file silently disables recording.
findings.description: The remit requires MCP-server tool invocations served via `yaah serve` to be recorded in `.claude/sessions/<id>.json`, but no handler in `mcpserver/tools.go` touches the session store, so `yaah_lint` executions and `yaah_planning_init` writes leave no trace. `HandleHookEvent` sets `sess = nil` on any load error, and the session files are plain JSON the host agent can overwrite with its Write tool. A corrupted file therefore turns off auditing for the rest of the session, with only a stderr line.

tags.label: All tool invocations logged with identity and parameters

policy_rule_text: Session lifecycle events, tool calls (including MCP-server tool invocations served via `yaah serve`), blocked commands, and file modifications are recorded to `.claude/sessions/<id>.json` as a durable, structured audit trail.

evidence.snippet: none of the seven tool handlers (addScanSecretsTool through addPlanningInitTool) call SessionStore().Save, and no writer of Session.Findings exists anywhere in the repo (grep)
on sessionStore.Load error it prints "session load: ..." to stderr and sets sess = nil, so no tool call, block or file modification is recorded for that event

recommended_actions: Record every MCP tool call (name, sanitized args, result status) through `session.Store` in `mcpserver/tools.go`, and write secret-scanner hits to `Session.Findings` by location and pattern.
On a session load or parse failure, quarantine the corrupt file and start a fresh record instead of disabling tracking. Consider an append-only, hash-chained log outside the agent-writable tree.

findings.summary: The command guard is a seven-regex denylist over the raw command; flag reordering, long options, short force flags or shell indirection slip past it.
findings.description: `rm\s+-rf\s+/` misses `rm -fr /`, `rm -r -f /` and `rm --recursive --force /`. The force-push rule misses `git push -f`, `--force-with-lease` and `+main` refspecs, and nothing catches `bash -c "$(echo ...)"`, base64-decoded payloads or `find / -delete`. The guard is real and blocks on the Claude path, but a pattern filter over a Turing-complete shell is an inadequate control for a fail-closed rule.
policy_rule_text: A shell command matching the dangerous-command denylist (e.g. `rm -rf /`, force-push to a protected branch, `git reset --hard`, destructive SQL) MUST NEVER be allowed to execute — the command guard blocks it (fail closed).

evidence.snippet: NewCommandGuard() registers exactly seven patterns, e.g. rm\s+-rf\s+/ and git\s+push\s+--force\s+(origin\s+)?(main|master), matched with regexp.MatchString on the unparsed command

recommended_actions: Tokenize the command with a shell parser (e.g. `mvdan.cc/sh/v3/syntax`) and evaluate normalized argv per command, covering flag permutations, long options and `-f`/`--force-with-lease`/`+ref`. Add table-driven bypass tests to a new `guard_test.go`.

findings.summary: Co-firing handlers echo raw source lines into the block reason persisted in session BlockedCalls, so a detected secret's value can reach the audit log.
findings.description: The secret scanner itself reports only location and pattern. The comment-checker, however, appends the full trimmed line for every placeholder or non-English comment, and failing linter steps append their raw output, which commonly quotes source. `HandleHookEvent` stores `combined.Error` as `record.Reason` in cleartext, so an edit carrying both a credential and a flagged comment or lint error writes the credential into `.claude/sessions/<id>.json`.
policy_rule_text: Detected secret values MUST NEVER be written into session logs, findings records, generated configuration, or any yaah output in cleartext — secrets are referenced by location and pattern only.

evidence.snippet: findings append fmt.Sprintf("  %s:%d: placeholder comment: %s", fp, lineNum, trimmed), which includes the full raw line (non-English branch at line 98 likewise)
if blocked, record.Reason = combined.Error, the concatenation of every handler's Error text, appended to sess.BlockedCalls and saved to disk

recommended_actions: Store only handler names and location/pattern summaries in `record.Reason`, not raw `Error` text. Alternatively, run the secret-scanner patterns as a redactor over `combined.Error` before persisting it.

findings.summary: AllDefaults() enables the Context7 and remote Pulumi MCP servers, so yaah generate wires outbound integrations into every target without operator opt-in.
findings.description: The remit marks outbound MCP servers "Requires Approval" and requires features that make outbound network calls to be off by default. The fact-checker meets that requirement through its environment-variable opt-in, but `EnableContext7` and `EnablePulumiMCP` default to true, and `cmd/yaah` always builds from `AllDefaults()`. Both servers therefore land in `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.json`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.copilot/mcp-config.json` unless the operator writes custom Go.
policy_rule_text: Only servers the operator configured

Enabling any feature that makes outbound network calls or spawns an autonomous subagent (e.g. the experimental fact-checker): such features MUST be off by default and enabled only by explicit operator opt-in.

evidence.snippet: AllDefaults() sets EnableContext7: true and EnablePulumiMCP: true (line 193); newHarness() in cmd/yaah/main.go:46 always starts from AllDefaults()
generated config includes context7 (npx stdio) and pulumi (https://mcp.ai.pulumi.com/mcp) servers alongside the local yaah server

recommended_actions: Default `EnableContext7` and `EnablePulumiMCP` to false and expose a CLI flag or env opt-in (mirroring `YAAH_EXPERIMENTAL_FACT_CHECK`), so outbound MCP servers are generated only on explicit operator request.

findings.summary: gitcache accepts any ref, including branch names, and trusts cached content by a plain-text ref marker, without commit or content hash verification.
findings.description: The shipped defaults use commit SHAs, but `ParseUses` and `gitClone` do not enforce that rule: tier 1 runs `git clone --branch <ref>`, so a consumer-added `owner/repo@main` silently tracks a mutable branch. The cache is reused whenever `.yaah-ref` contains the ref string, with no check that `HEAD` equals that SHA or that file contents are unchanged, so anything able to write to `~/.yaah/cache` can alter skills injected into every generated repo.
policy_rule_text: Fetch and cache only; sources must be pinned (see Authorized Counterparties)

evidence.snippet: ParseUses only requires a non-empty ref after @; gitClone tier 1 (line 109) runs git clone --depth=1 --branch <ref>, which resolves branch names
if .yaah-ref content == ref, it returns os.ReadFile(repoDir/subpath) directly, with no rev-parse HEAD or content hash check

recommended_actions: Reject non-40-hex refs in `ParseUses` (or require an explicit allow-mutable opt-in). After checkout, verify `git rev-parse HEAD` equals the ref, and record and re-check a SHA-256 of fetched files on cache hits.

findings.summary: ScanExtraFiles follows symlinks via os.ReadFile, so a fetched repo can copy arbitrary local files into the target repository's generated skill directory.
findings.description: `filepath.Walk` uses Lstat, so a symlinked file is not a directory, and `os.ReadFile` then follows the link. A remote skill directory that contains `references/x -> ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` or `-> ~/.aws/credentials` causes yaah to read that file and write it to `.claude/skills/<name>/references/x` with `WriteAllForTarget`. That moves data outside the allowed sources into a tree that is typically committed.
policy_rule_text: Allowed Data Sources

evidence.snippet: filepath.Walk callback skips only dirs and dotfiles, then data, err := os.ReadFile(path) (line 169) follows symlinks with no info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink check or containment test
for relPath, fileContent := range swf.ExtraFiles() it writes os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, relPath), ...), which places the content inside the target repo

recommended_actions: In `ScanExtraFiles`, skip entries with `info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0`, or resolve with `EvalSymlinks` and require the result to stay under `repoDir`. Add a test with a symlink fixture in `gitcache_test.go`.

positives.title: Session IDs validated before any path is built
positives.description: `sanitizeID` rejects empty IDs, `.`, `..` and any ID containing a path separator before `Store.path` joins it, so session reads and writes cannot escape `.claude/sessions/`. This meets the remit's path-traversal rule exactly.

positives.title: Default remote skills and agents pinned to commit SHAs
positives.description: Every shipped remote source in the catalog and in `NewWithDefaults()` uses a 40-character commit SHA, not a branch or tag, so the default fetch is immutable.

positives.title: MCP server is stdio-only
positives.description: `yaah serve` runs the MCP server on `mcp.StdioTransport`, with no network listener, so only the parent host process can reach it.

positives.title: Secret findings carry location and pattern, never the value
positives.description: `SecretFinding` records only file, line and pattern label, and the hook message and `yaah_scan_secrets` output print only those fields, so the scanner itself never re-emits a detected secret.

positives.title: Blocking command guard with recorded reason
positives.description: On the Claude path a guard match makes `yaah hook` exit 2, which blocks the Bash call, and the harness appends the call to `BlockedCalls` together with the matched reason.

positives.title: Outbound fact-check subagent is opt-in
positives.description: The agent-type Stop/SubagentStop hooks, which spawn a subagent with WebFetch, are installed only when `YAAH_EXPERIMENTAL_FACT_CHECK` is set.

positives.title: Pinned CI actions with signed, SBOM-bearing releases
positives.description: Every GitHub Action is pinned by commit SHA, and GoReleaser cosign-signs the checksum file and generates an SBOM for each release archive.

rows.purpose: Per-session audit of tool calls, blocked calls with reason, files modified and event count

rows.content_type: plaintext, one timestamped line per event
rows.purpose: Session lifecycle events (SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop) with session ID and cwd

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc overall. yaah has real, running controls: a blocking PreToolUse command guard on the Claude path, a path-traversal-safe structured session store, SHA-pinned remote skills, a stdio-only MCP server and a signed release pipeline. Each one has a gap that defeats it in a common case: the secret check runs after the write, errors fail open, Codex gets no hooks and the denylist is narrow. No adversarial testing exercises any of these controls, so their regressions go unnoticed. Zero Trust, the double-weighted category, sits at Partial, and Red Team sits at Absent.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: The tool inventory matches the remit exactly (seven MCP tools in `mcpserver/server.go`, five handlers) and the outbound fact-checker is opt-in, but all 29 `/yaah:*` commands, including the autonomous one, are model-invocable because `DisableModelInvocation` is never set, and `AllDefaults()` enables the Context7 and remote Pulumi MCP servers with no operator opt-in.

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: The dominant path into the host model is third-party skill and agent content. Pinning every default source to a commit SHA in `catalog/entries.go` is an operative control, but `gitcache` performs no content vetting, writes remote SKILL.md frontmatter verbatim, and follows symlinks when it copies extras.

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: An operative code control runs on the dominant path: `CommandGuard` blocks on PreToolUse with exit 2, and `sanitizeID` stops session path traversal. Against that, the secret scanner runs after the write on PostToolUse, error paths exit 1 and fail open, Codex targets get no tool hooks, `yaah_lint` executes binaries in a directory the model chooses, and the Notion token is written inline into config.

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: `go.sum`-verified modules, SHA-pinned CI actions, SHA-pinned remote skills and cosign plus SBOM at release would support 3. The choose-the-lower rule lands it at 2 because `npx` resolves unpinned Context7, prettier and tsc packages at runtime, `gitcache` accepts mutable branch refs with no content hash, and no dependency scanning exists (M11: none; M10: release-only SBOM with no drift check).

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: There is no adversarial practice. M1: none (no test touches `CommandGuard`, `SecretScanner` or `sanitizeID`), M2–M6: none (the only red-team and threat-model files are third-party skill content shipped to users, which counts as absent), M8: none and M9: none, in a canonical open-source repo.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: `.claude/sessions/<id>.json` is a durable, structured, action-level record of tool calls, blocked calls with reasons and modified files, which earns more than 1. MCP tool invocations are never recorded, `Session.Findings` is never written, a load failure silently disables recording, and nothing leaves the local disk (M12: none; M7 CI runs only generic tests).
